items.title: Anne Phillips interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, February 24, 2025
items.q: I was working with Charlie Calello who did all the Four Seasons stuff you know, and other stuff, and the record dates were well written, were good stuff and fun.

ctx.x: One last thing with this. Chico Hamilton talked about, you know he did this for 15 or 20 years, and he — this is a quote from him. He says, “I started in ’66 until the 80s maybe. I learned how to drink in the daytime, the three martini lunch, and how to schmooze. I made a lot of dough but what good is the dough when you kind of lose something.” So do you know, what is that something that he would have felt?

I certainly know it about guys that went into Broadway. Because Broadway gig was like the bottom of the barrel during that time when there were record dates and so forth. And then when those dates began to go away and people began to take Broadway jobs they lost something and they talked about losing that something. And you know I was fortunate because I was writing most of what I did. I mean I did the first record dates, of course all record dates were wonderful, but I was working with Charlie Calello who did…
